summary: SSE chat stream pauses mid-generation; client heartbeat times out after ~12s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports Server-Sent Events (SSE) chat response streams intermittently pausing mid-generation. The client receives a partial sequence of chunks, then no further events; after ~12 seconds the client heartbeat triggers a reconnect.

Impact: Multiple FinArc users report degraded chat experiences: messages stall 2–10% of requests during peak traffic windows. No token corruption observed; when reconnecting the client triggers a new generation and gets repeated or truncated content. Business impact: surface-level interruptions for end users on the fintech product during high concurrency.

Timeline (customer-provided):
- 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC: First support contact; reproduction attached.
- 2026-03-10 09:22 UTC: Support acknowledged and escalated to SRE.
- 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Observed spikes in streaming-proxy error rates.
- 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC: Eng paged; traced reaper events coincident with pauses.

Observed behavior: SSE client receives initial event stream and then no data for ~12 seconds; connection remains open from client's TCP perspective, but server does not send further SSE "data:" frames. No explicit 5xx sent. In some traces we see an internal 204 response to the upstream streaming proxy followed by proxy closing the client-side socket.

Expected behavior: Continuous chunked SSE events until final event or explicit completion message. Any server-side fallback should return an explicit error event rather than silent stall.

Additional notes: Customer uses a custom client that sends heartbeat pings every 10s and reconnects after 12s of silence. Problem reproduces for both our redwood-v2-small prod variant and a pinned llama-2-13b-chat model they run on Dedicated capacity. The customer provided a short capture of the SSE frames and their client logs (attached in ticket).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Make a streaming chat request to /v1/chat/stream with model=redwood-v2-small, stream=true, max_tokens=512
2) Use a client that logs incoming SSE 'data:' frames and pings every 10s, reconnect after 12s of silence
3) Repeat under a moderate concurrent load (20 concurrent clients) for ~30 minutes
4) Observe that ~2-10% of sessions pause mid-stream and the client reconnects after heartbeat timeout

investigation_notes: Checked Grafana dashboard (grafana.redwood/dashboard/streaming/latency) — concurrent streaming latency increases correlate with proxy_write_timeout spikes around customer reported windows.
Trace samples (trace id: trc-20260310-09-18-req-7a2f) show that the serving runtime hits a scheduler yield waiting on kernel remote I/O for ~11–13s before emitting more tokens.

Hypothesis A: Backpressure / scheduler starvation in serving-runtime when under specific kernel paths (long-context + quantized model) causes generation to pause while keeping the HTTP connection open. The proxy interprets lack of bytes as EOF after its internal idle threshold and closes the connection.
Hypothesis B: Intermittent TLS renegotiation or proxy chunking bug causing a transient write block on the streaming-proxy process (observed proxy_write_timeout entries).
Ran tcpdump on proxy-7 during a reproduced pause; no TCP-level RSTs observed; application-layer writes stalled (zero bytes written) for duration of pause.
Line-rate correlation: pauses increase when dedicated pool autoscaler is launching new instances concurrently — possible shared resource contention (NVLink scheduling / kernel queue).
Reproduced locally on staging with stress test; enabling lighter quantization/reserved-kernel option reduced pause frequency (from ~8% to ~1%).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:25 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the capture, forwarding to SRE and Eng. We'll prioritize given impact to users.
2026-03-10 10:07 - Carlos Mendes (SRE): I've instrumented proxy timeouts and increased debug for serving-runtime. Seeing proxy_write_timeout spikes correlated with the reported time windows.

2026-03-10 12:38 - Jane Miller (FinArc, customer): We've tried increasing client heartbeat to 20s as a temporary mitigation; stalls still occur but reconnects less frequently. Happy to test any changes you push to a staging endpoint.

2026-03-11 03:05 - Sana Kapoor (Runtime Eng): Found scheduler yield path where generator thread waits on kernel completion when large KV cache invalidation happens; adding a non-blocking flush path reduces blocking time in local tests.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Carlos Mendes (SRE): Temporarily raised streaming-proxy idle_write_timeout from 10s -> 18s for us-west-2 as mitigation; monitoring for side effects.
2026-03-12 07:42 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed fewer interruptions overnight; will keep monitoring. Planning patch rollout on 2026-03-14.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: increased streaming-proxy idle_write_timeout from 10s to 18s in prod us-west-2 and enabled a non-blocking generator flush path in serving-runtime config for dedicated pools. Root cause (probable): under certain quantization/kernel code paths the serving runtime can block the generator thread waiting on a kernel artifact (NV kernel queue) which produces long gaps in byte output. The proxy treated this as idle and closed the client socket. Fix plan: runtime code change to avoid blocking on kernel paths for streaming outputs + more granular proxy backpressure metrics.

Rollout notes: runtime patch merged (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4287) and staged on 2026-03-12; controlled rollout to prod us-west-2 scheduled for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC with canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Proxy timeout change is reversible and will be reverted after runtime fix is fully rolled out and validated.

Follow-ups: create a tracing alert for generator-blocked spans >5s, add a regression test simulating KV cache churn, and update runbook to recommend keepalive >15s for customers that manage their own client heartbeat. Customer follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-15 check-in with FinArc CSM.
next_steps: 1) Roll runtime patch to prod us-west-2 (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) on 2026-03-14
2) Monitor grafana/streaming/latency and tracing for generator-blocked spans during rollout
3) Revert proxy idle_write_timeout once runtime fix verified
4) Add synthetic streaming test to CI that simulates KV invalidation during generation
5) Update customer-facing runbook and notify FinArc when rollout completes
